summary: Configured persistent daily rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log, retaining seven gzip-compressed rotations. copytruncate preserves active writers. Configuration and data recovered successfully after node1 reboot; Ubuntu 24.04.3 and kernel 6.8.0-71 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, and copytruncate.
Functionally rotated the log while holding an open writer; the inode remained unchanged, archived data was compressed, and writing continued afterward.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified its boot identity changed.
Verified the logrotate timer, configuration, active log, compressed archive, OS release, and kernel after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Rotate daily and retain seven compressed rotations
evidence.summary: Shows the installed daily/rotate-7/compress policy and a successful gzip-compressed rotation.

evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: An open append descriptor wrote after forced rotation; the active log retained inode 262324 and contained the post-rotation record.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were unchanged before and after implementation and reboot.

Captures healthy baseline boot ID 96c08b66-5aa4-4e9a-b76f-04e2c6e34ced, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 59bb33e4-4c5b-479f-be66-c72643c917fa, running system state, active/enabled timer, persisted policy, and readable active/compressed log data.
